anti_overlap: Focuses on dynamic detail adaptation from game rendering, not compression (medical) or serialization (accessibility)
decision_lens: Balances visual fidelity against frame budget — the right detail level is the one that achieves the task without exceeding the budget
distance_rationale: Both domains dynamically choose visual detail levels to fit within a performance budget, but game engines have mature frameworks for this tradeoff.
expected_isomorphisms: LOD selection, temporal coherence, and budget allocation directly map to adaptive terminal state encoding.
focus: Level-of-detail rendering — dynamic fidelity based on distance, importance, and performance budget
name: fd-game-rendering-lod
persona: Game engine rendering engineer who implements LOD systems, impostor sprites, and performance-adaptive rendering pipelines
review_areas: LOD selection — choosing detail level based on importance/distance (maps to: choosing terminal state detail based on agent task and context budget)
Impostor rendering — replacing complex 3D objects with 2D sprites when far away (maps to: replacing complex terminal regions with text summaries)
Occlusion culling — not rendering what's behind other objects (maps to: not encoding terminal regions covered by popups/dialogs)
Temporal coherence — reusing previous frame data when little has changed (maps to: diff-based terminal updates)
Performance budget allocation — distributing render budget to most important objects first (maps to: distributing token budget to most important terminal regions)

severity_examples.condition: Every terminal capture costs maximum tokens regardless of task complexity
severity_examples.scenario: No LOD system — always maximum detail

severity_examples.condition: Agent notices quality jumps between detail levels and gets confused

source_domain: Game engine rendering (LOD, occlusion culling, performance budgets)
success_hints: Proposes a multi-level detail system where the terminal state representation scales with the agent's current needs
task_context: Game engines solved the 'too much visual detail for the budget' problem with LOD. Terminal state for LLMs has the same constraint: context window is the frame budget.
